headline: Elevator Passengers Trapped 'Between Floors 12 and 14' for Eight Hours
subheadline: Omnicorp Holdings issues statement dismissing reports of 'temporal anomalies' as 'mass hysteria'
summary: Seven people were trapped in a Hartwell Building elevator that apparently stopped at a floor that officially does not exist, with passengers reporting disturbing time discrepancies.
content:
Seven individuals spent what they claim was eight hours trapped in the Hartwell Building's east elevator last Thursday evening, though building management insists the incident lasted "no more than 47 minutes."

The elevator, traveling from the lobby to the 14th floor, reportedly stopped between floors 12 and 14. Emergency responders noted the unusual nature of the call.

"The panel said floor 13," explained Fire Captain Rodriguez. "But according to the building schematics, there is no floor 13. Never has been. The building goes 12, 14. Like most buildings that age."

Passengers tell a different story. According to software developer Priya Sharma, 31, the elevator doors opened briefly onto what she described as "an office floor, but wrong."

"The lights were flickering in a pattern," Sharma said. "There were desks, but the proportions were... I don't know how to explain it. Everything was slightly too long. And there was static. Not from speakers. The air itself was static."

Another passenger, Derek Observerson, a local quantum coffee enthusiast, attempted to document the phenomenon but found his phone's camera would only display error messages. "Jennifer always said I was paranoid," he muttered to reporters. "But I know what I saw in those mirrors."

Omnicorp Holdings, the building's managing company, released a statement attributing the incident to "routine maintenance" and "mass hysteria likely induced by the confined space." They declined to comment on why the elevator panel includes a button for floor 13 if no such floor exists.

The city's building inspector has announced plans to investigate the property next week. Meanwhile, three of the seven passengers have reportedly begun meeting regularly at a coffee shop to compare notes. They have requested anonymity due to what they describe as "concerned emails from addresses ending in @omnicorp.internal."
author: Tom Hendricks, City Hall Reporter
